name: Commercial and Market Access
blurb: AI in pharma sales, CRM, customer engagement, real world evidence and deals.
title: Commercial and Market Access
answer: Commercial teams were early adopters of AI agents: CRM vendors built life sciences agents for field sales and medical liaisons, and several of the largest drugmakers chose new AI based engagement platforms in 2025 and 2026. AI is also used to analyse real world evidence for market access.

reading.body:
Commercial teams in pharma adopted AI agents before most other functions, and the largest drugmakers consolidated on shared platforms rather than building their own.

The pattern is consolidation. Novartis and AstraZeneca both selected Salesforce Agentforce Life Sciences in December 2025, and Chiesi Group followed in April 2026. Salesforce reported more than 140 life sciences organizations on the same product. Field sales, medical liaisons, and customer engagement are the entry point, with real world evidence analysis for market access close behind.

This matters for AI because it shows where regulated industries actually deploy agents first. The constraint is not model capability but review. Promotional content and interactions with health care professionals fall under the same medical, legal, and regulatory approval whether a person or an agent produces them, so the winning vendors are the ones that put that review inside the workflow.

The data covers platform choices and adoption counts, not outcomes. It does not say whether these deployments improved sales, reduced cost, or shortened review cycles, and it does not cover the compute or infrastructure behind them.
